summary.text: Mariannette Miller-Meeks is the Republican incumbent for Iowa's 1st District, seeking a fourth term. A physician and U.S. Army veteran, she ran unsuccessfully for Congress three times before winning in 2020 by six votes, and previously led the Iowa Department of Public Health and served in the Iowa Senate. She is running on her record in Congress, including her work on health care and veterans' issues.

paragraphs.text: Miller-Meeks was born in Herlong, California (September 6, 1955, according to Wikipedia). According to her official biography, she was the fourth of eight children and left home at 16 to attend community college.

She earned a bachelor's degree in nursing from Texas Christian University (1976), a master's degree from the University of Southern California (1980), and a medical degree from the University of Texas Health Science Center (1986).

She served in the U.S. Army for 24 years as a private, nurse, and doctor, according to her official biography; Wikipedia lists active duty from 1976 to 1982 and Army Reserve service from 1983 until she retired in 2000.

According to Wikipedia, she practiced as an ophthalmologist, running a private practice in Ottumwa, Iowa, until 2008, and was the first woman in two decades on the University of Iowa ophthalmology faculty.

Miller-Meeks was the Republican nominee for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District in 2008, 2010, and 2014, losing to Democrat Dave Loebsack each time. Gov. Terry Branstad appointed her director of the Iowa Department of Public Health, a post she held from 2010 to 2014.
She was elected to the Iowa Senate (District 41) in 2018 and served until January 2021, when she resigned to join the U.S. House.

Miller-Meeks won the 2020 race for the 2nd District by six votes after a recount over Democrat Rita Hart, who later withdrew a challenge to the result. She won re-election in the renumbered 1st District in 2022 (53.4 percent) and in 2024 (by 799 votes after a recount), both over Christina Bohannan.

She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its Health subcommittee, and on the Veterans' Affairs Committee, where she chairs the Health Subcommittee. According to her official biography, she has two grown children.
She won the June 2026 Republican primary over David Pautsch.

sources.title: Independent candidate enters 'toss up' race for 1st Congressional District
